distractors.reason: We don't say 'believe at'. 'At' is used for points in space or time, as in look at or arrive at.
We don't say 'believe on'. 'On' is used with depend on, rely on and focus on.
We don't say 'believe for'. 'For' follows verbs such as wait for, ask for and look for.

example_sentence: Thomas Edison always believed ___ his ideas, even after many failures.
l1_interference: Los hispanohablantes suelen omitir la preposición y dicen 'believe his ideas', como en 'creer a alguien' o 'creo tus ideas'. En inglés, cuando hablamos de confiar en una idea o persona, siempre usamos 'believe in'.
explanation: In English, 'believe in' means to trust a person or to be confident that an idea or a thing is good. It needs the preposition 'in', even when Spanish does not use one.

related_collocations.example: The success of the invention depends on the weather.
Please wait for me here while I get the tools.

memory_tip: BELIEVE IN = trust a person or an idea (believe in yourself) | BELIEVE = accept that something is true (I believe you)
